import sys

def changes_for_one(s: str) -> int:
    n = len(s)
    cnt = 0
    i = 0
    while i < n:
        j = i
        while j < n and s[j] == s[i]:
            j += 1
        cnt += (j - i) // 2
        i = j
    return cnt

def main():
    data = sys.stdin.read().strip().split()
    s = data[0]
    k = int(data[1])

    # If all characters are the same, the whole concatenation is one run.
    if len(set(s)) == 1:
        print((len(s) * k) // 2)
        return

    # If first and last characters differ, copies do not merge across boundaries.
    if s[0] != s[-1]:
        print(changes_for_one(s) * k)
        return

    # First and last characters are the same, so boundary runs merge.
    n = len(s)

    # Prefix run length of s[0]
    a = 0
    while a < n and s[a] == s[0]:
        a += 1

    # Suffix run length of s[-1]
    b = 0
    while b < n and s[n - 1 - b] == s[-1]:
        b += 1

    one = changes_for_one(s)

    # Extra contribution for each boundary merge:
    # floor((a+b)/2) - floor(a/2) - floor(b/2)
    extra = (a + b) // 2 - a // 2 - b // 2

    print(one * k + extra * (k - 1))

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
